target_claim: The explicit (<=)-direction crossing schedule -- Initial Trip carrying all of the cover C from left to right, then K Cover Delivery Rounds (Trip A: carry C\{c_i} right->left leaving c_i alone; Trip B: carry C\{c_i} left->right), then a Final Stage in which 'Charon can return empty (or with some non-conflicting passenger) to the left bank, then load up to K passengers from L1 and ferry them to the right bank' -- is claimed to be a valid sequence of crossings with boat capacity k = K+1, with the invariant (lines 0103-0105): 'This procedure produces a valid sequence of crossings using boat capacity k = K + 1. At every point, the bank without Charon holds either an independent set of H's vertices or is empty.'
failing_input: H = P4, the path a-b-c-d on vertices {0,1,2,3} with edges (0,1),(1,2),(2,3); vertex cover C = {1,2} = {b,c} (a MINIMUM vertex cover of P4, |C| = K = 2); reduction sets G = H, k = K+1 = 3; L1 = V\C = {0,3}. The solution's schedule is: trip1 L->R {1,2}; trip2 R->L {2}; trip3 L->R {2}; trip4 R->L {1}; trip5 L->R {1}; trip6 R->L (empty); trip7 L->R {0,3}. It fails at trip 6. The same failure occurs on the triage's other named instances: K3 (C={0,1}, k=3, fails at trip 6), K4 (C={0,1,2}, k=4, fails at trip 8), K5 (C={0,1,2,3}, k=5, fails at trip 10).
observed_vs_claimed: CLAIMED: the generated schedule is a valid sequence of crossings and at every point the Charon-free bank induces no edge of H. OBSERVED (exact simulator, Oracle #1): on H = P4 with C = {b,c}, trip 6 is the Final Stage's 'Charon returns empty' trip; when Charon departs the right bank it holds C = {1,2} = {b,c} unsupervised, and (1,2) = (b,c) is an edge of H -- two enemies alone together, violating the problem's safety condition and directly falsifying the quoted invariant. This is a rest-state violation as well as an in-transit one (after trip 6 completes, Charon is at rest on the left and the right bank still holds {b,c}), so it is independent of whether one checks safety mid-crossing. Oracle #2, an exhaustive BFS over the full state space, shows a valid crossing sequence for this very instance DOES exist (L->R {0,2}; R->L empty; L->R {1,3}), so the defect is in the constructed schedule and its invariant, not in the decision-level answer for this instance. Exhaustive search over ALL graphs on n = 4, 5, 6 vertices with at least one edge, using K = size of a minimum vertex cover, k = K+1, and running the schedule for EVERY minimum cover of H: the schedule is invalid for at least one minimum cover on 56/63 (88.9%) of n=4 graphs, 1022/1023 (99.9%) of n=5 graphs, 32360/32767 (98.8%) of n=6 graphs; it is invalid for EVERY minimum cover on 42/63, 1019/1023 and 30487/32767 respectively. The solution's parenthetical escape hatch does not help: enumerating EVERY legal return load (any subset of the right bank of size <= K, which covers 'or with some non-conflicting passenger') yields no valid schedule for K3, K4, K5 or for P4 with C={b,c} -- every choice either leaves an enemy pair unsupervised or ends with a passenger stranded on the left bank. BONUS (strictly stronger, found by the same oracles): the reduction's (<=) direction fails at the DECISION level too. For H = the star K_{1,3} (edges (0,1),(0,2),(0,3)), the minimum vertex cover is {0} so K = 1 and k = K+1 = 2; exhaustive BFS proves NO valid crossing sequence exists, refuting lines 0106-0107 ('if H has a vertex cover of size K, then the river crossing problem with G = H and k = K+1 is solvable') and hence the Conclusion's biconditional. Such instances occur at every size tested (n = 4, 5, 6).
faithfulness_notes: The schedule was implementable exactly as written; nothing load-bearing was invented. Details: (1) Cover size -- the solution says (line 0038) 'WLOG assume |C| = K (pad C with arbitrary extra vertices if |C| < K)', so K := |C| is used and no padding is ever needed. (2) Cover ordering -- C = {c1,...,cK} is taken in the solution's own labelling order (sorted vertex order); the failure is order-independent and, on most instances, cover-independent (see the 'INVALID for EVERY minimum cover' counts). (3) An internal inconsistency in the text was resolved in the solution's favour: line 0077 asserts c_i 'remains permanently on the right bank (Charon never brought c_i back)', but the explicitly specified Trip A of round i+1 loads C\{c_(i+1)}, which contains c_i, and does bring it back. The explicit trip loads were implemented as written; this does not affect the counterexample, which lies in the Final Stage after all rounds are done and all of C is on the right. (4) Final Stage -- the literal text 'Charon can return empty ... then load up to K passengers from L1' is the primary implementation; the parenthetical 'or with some non-conflicting passenger' is covered by a generous variant that tries every legal return load. (5) Trip semantics -- while the boat is on the water neither bank has Charon, so both must induce no edge; on arrival the abandoned bank must still induce no edge; enemies may share Charon's own bank. This is the only reading consistent with the problem statement, and the counterexample survives the weaker rest-states-only reading as well. (6) Edgeless graphs H are excluded from the sweep because they give K = 0 and k = 1, a degenerate instance in which the boat cannot carry any passenger; that is a separate (also fatal) gap in the reduction, not the target claim. (7) All computation is exact set/integer arithmetic; no floats, no randomness, no wall-clock timing; output is deterministic.
